title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Martín Antolínez and Muño Gustioz challenge; envoys of Navarre and Aragon arrive (tiradas 144–149, lines 3329–3408)
part: Tiradas 144–149 · Martín Antolínez and Muño Gustioz challenge; envoys of Navarre and Aragon arrive (lines 3329–3408)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 333–339, lines 3329–3408 (tiradas 144–149). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Di, Ferrando, otorga esta razón:
¿non te viene en miente en Valençia lo del león
quando durmie mio Çid y el león se desató?
sentences.l:
Say, Ferrando, confess this matter:
not to-you comes in mind in Valençia the-business of-the lion
when was-sleeping my Çid and the lion itself untied?
sentences.i: Speak, Fernando, own to this: do you not remember, in Valencia, the business of the lion, when my Çid lay asleep and the lion broke loose?
sentences.n: Tirada 144 (assonance ó) — Per Vermudoz's challenge goes on (Pidal: Prosigue el reto de Pedro Vermúdez). The line-ends run razón, león, desató, pavor, Campeador, oy, señor …: stressed ó, with ó-e in varones (v. 3347). There is no new speech: Per Vermudoz, who began in tirada 143, still speaks to Fernando with tú. Di, 'say', imperative of dezir. otorga, imperative of otorgar, here 'confess, own'. Pidal's note to v. 3329: otorga esta razón, 'confiesa esto' — '"confess this"'. razón, 'matter, statement'. Pidal's note to v. 3330: non te viene en miente, 'no se te acuerda?' — '"do you not remember?"'. lo del león, 'the business of the lion': the escape of the Çid's lion in Valencia, told in tirada 112 (vv. 2278–2301). durmie, imperfect of dormir, 'was sleeping'. y, 'and' (as i in v. 2; usually e). se desató, 'got loose', literally 'untied itself'.

sentences.t:
E tú, Ferrando, ¿qué fizist con el pavor?
¡metístet tras el escaño de mio Çid el Campeador!
metístet Ferrando, por o menos vales oy.
sentences.l:
And you, Ferrando, what did-you-do with the fear?
you-put-yourself behind the bench of my Çid the Campeador!
you-put-yourself Ferrando, through which less you-are-worth today.
sentences.i: And you, Fernando, what did you do in your fright? You crept behind the bench of my Çid the Campeador! You hid there, Fernando, and for that you are worth less today, a dishonoured man.
sentences.n: fizist = fiziste (modern hiciste), 'you did', with the final -e dropped. con el pavor, 'with the fear', in your terror. metístet = metiste + te, 'you put yourself', you hid. At v. 2287 Fernando crept sol esçaño, 'under the bench'; here he is tras el escaño, 'behind' it. escaño, 'bench' (house). Pidal prints ¿ … ? and ¡ … ! here, as shown. por o = por + o, 'through which, whereby' (o, 'where', as at v. 2618). menos vales, 'you are worth less' (house: 'worth less, dishonoured'), the charge of tirada 139 made again.

sentences.i: We closed round the bench to guard our lord, until my Çid awoke, he who won Valencia; he rose from the bench and went toward the lion;
sentences.n: Nós, 'we', the stressed pronoun: the Çid's men, Per Vermudoz among them (v. 2285, çercan el escaño). curiar, 'guard, keep' (= curar, cuidar). fasta do, 'until': Pidal's note to v. 3336: 'hasta que despertó' — '"until he awoke"'. gañó = ganó, 'won'. levantós = levantó + se, 'rose'. f[o]s = fo + se, 'went off' (fo = fue), the o Pidal's. poral = pora + el, 'toward the'.

sentences.t:
el león premió la cabeça, a mio Çid esperó,
dexósle prender al cuello, e a la red le metió.
sentences.l:
the lion lowered the head, for my Çid it-waited,
let-itself-him take by-the neck, and into the cage it he-put.
sentences.i: the lion bowed its head and waited for my Çid, let him take it by the neck, and he put it back in its cage.
sentences.n: premió, 'lowered', preterite of premer (Pidal 'bajó'), as at v. 2299; not modern premiar. a mio Çid esperó, 'waited for my Çid', with the a of a person as object. dexósle prender = dexó + se + le, 'let itself be taken by him': Pidal's note to v. 3339: 'dejó que él le cogiese por el cuello' — '"it let him take it by the neck"'. The subject changes without warning: the lion lets itself be taken, the Çid puts it in. la red, 'the net', the cage (as at vv. 2282, 2301).

sentences.i: When the good Campeador turned round, he saw his vassals all about him; he asked for his sons-in-law, and found neither one!
sentences.n: se tornó, 'turned round, turned back'. a sos vassallos, víolos, 'his vassals, he saw them': the object put first, with the a of persons, and taken up by los (víolos = vio + los). That is our reading of Pidal's comma after Campeador; the line could also be read 'turned back to his vassals'. aderredor, 'round about'. demandó por, 'asked after'. s[o]s, the o Pidal's. ninguno non falló, 'he found none': the double negative, normal in Old Spanish.

sentences.t:
Riébtot el cuerpo por malo e por traidor.
Éstot lidiaré aquí ante rey don Alfons
por fijas del Çid, don Elvira e doña Sol:
sentences.i: I challenge you in your own person as a wicked man and a traitor. This I will maintain against you in combat, here before King Alfonso, for the Çid's daughters, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol:
sentences.n: Riébtot = riebto + te, 'I challenge you' (riebto, house 'challenge'). Pidal's note to v. 3343: Riébtot el cuerpo, literalmente, 'te reto tu persona'. era fórmula del reto, v. 3442, así como la que indicamos a propósito del verso siguiente — 'literally, "I challenge you your person". It was a formula of the challenge, v. 3442, like the one we point out at the next line' (the small e of era as printed). por malo e por traidor, 'as wicked and as traitor'. Éstot = esto + te. Pidal's note to v. 3344: 'Esto te lidiaré'; lidiar significa aquí 'sustentar por medio de una lid judicial, una acusación'. Era fórmula consagrada para el reto decir al retado: esto te lidiaré, esto lidiaré, 3359 b, o bien yo te lo lidiaré (yollo lidiaré, 3367, lidiártelo, he, ego tibi litiabo) — '"This I will fight against you"; lidiar here means "to uphold an accusation by means of a judicial combat". It was the hallowed formula of the challenge to say to the challenged man: esto te lidiaré, esto lidiaré (3359b), or yo te lo lidiaré (yollo lidiaré, 3367; lidiártelo he, punctuated lidiártelo, he on the page; Latin ego tibi litiabo)'. ante rey don Alfons, 'before King Alfonso', without the article. por fijas del Çid, 'on behalf of the Çid's daughters'. don Elvira, as printed, 'Doña Elvira' (house).

sentences.i: Because you abandoned them, you are worth less, dishonoured men; they are women and you are men, yet in every way they are worth more than you.
sentences.n: por quanto, 'inasmuch as, because'. dexastes, menos valedes, sodes: the speaker turns from Fernando (tú) to both Infantes (vos, plural). menos valedes, 'you are worth less' (house: 'worth less, dishonoured'). mugieres = mujeres. varones, 'men', in the full sense of grown men of worth; its ó-e still chimes with the ó of the tirada. en todas guisas, 'in every way'. Pidal's note to v. 3377 points back to this line: the Infantes could not bear that the Çid's daughters should be worth more than they.

sentences.i: When the combat comes, if it please the Creator, you will confess it as a traitor must; and I shall be proved true in all that I have said.”
sentences.n: f[o]re = fuere, future subjunctive of ser, 'shall be', the o Pidal's; ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer, 'if it shall please'. lid, 'fight', here the judicial combat. Back to tú: otorgarás, 'you will confess'. Pidal's note to v. 3350: 'tu lo confesarás'. El vencido debia confesar con su boca que tenia razón el vencedor, o debía perder la vida, Por esto el acusador dice al retar: por tu boca lo dirás que eres traydor, 3370, o bien fazértelo he dezir, 3389 — '"you will confess it". The beaten man had to confess with his own mouth that the victor was in the right, or lose his life. So the accuser says, when he challenges: por tu boca lo dirás que eres traydor (3370), or fazértelo he dezir (3389)'. (Accents and punctuation as printed: the first debia and tenia without an accent, the second debía with one; a comma, not a full stop, before Por.) Pidal goes on: a man who publicly took back his words said 'I lied by this mouth'; the confession may be indirect, and in this poem it is enough for the beaten man to say, himself or through one authorised, vençudo so 'I am beaten' (3644, 3691), or to leave the field (3667). a guisa de traydor, 'in the manner of a traitor'. verdadero seré yo, 'I shall be truthful', shown to have spoken the truth. The speech ends here.

sentences.t: D' aquestos amos aquí quedó la razón.
sentences.l: Of these both here stopped the talk.
sentences.i: Between these two the matter rested there.
sentences.n: D' aquestos amos, 'of these two' (aquestos = estos; amos = ambos): Per Vermudoz and Fernando. quedó, 'stopped, came to rest' (quedar). razón, 'talk, matter'. Fernando makes no answer. The singer closes the exchange, and v. 3372 closes the next one with the same words.

sentences.t:
Dí[a]g Gonçál[v]ez odredes lo que dixo:
“De natura somos de los co[m]des más li[n]pios;
sentences.l:
Dí[a]g Gonçál[v]ez you-shall-hear what he-said:
“Of birth we-are of the counts most pure;
sentences.i: Hear now what Diego González said: “By birth we are of the purest line of counts;
sentences.n: Tirada 145 (assonance í-o) — Diego rejects the charge of being worth less (Pidal: Diego desecha la inculpación de menos-valer). The line-ends run dixo, li[n]pios, apareçidos, Rodrigo, repentimos, sospiros …: stressed í, then o. Dí[a]g Gonçál[v]ez, 'Diego González' (house), the a and v Pidal's; his name stands first, outside the sentence: 'Diego González, you will hear what he said'. odredes = oiredes, future of oír, the singer to his hearers. natura, 'birth, lineage'. co[m]des, li[n]pios, the m and n Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 3354: linpios 'ilustres, puros, de limpia sangre' — '"illustrious, pure, of clean blood"'. Diego repeats Fernando's boast of v. 3296.

sentences.t:
¡estos casamientos non fuessen apareçidos,
por consagrar con mio Çid don Rodrigo!
sentences.l:
these marriages not had-been brought-about,
for to-become-kin with my Çid don Rodrigo!
sentences.i: would that these marriages had never been made, to bind us in kinship with my Çid Don Rodrigo!
sentences.n: non fuessen apareçidos, 'would they had not come about': a wish in the past, with ser as the auxiliary of an intransitive verb (apareçer). Pidal's note to v. 3355: non fuessen aparecidos, 'no se hubiesen efectuado' — '"would they had not been carried out"' (the headword printed without the cedilla). consagrar, 'become kin by marriage': Pidal's note to v. 3356: consagrar, 'emparentar', véase 1906 — '"to become related", see v. 1906' (por conssagrar con iffantes de Carrión). Even Diego says mio Çid, the poem's fixed name for the hero.

sentences.i: We do not repent, even now, that we abandoned his daughters; as long as they live they may well sigh: what we did to them will be thrown in their faces.
sentences.n: Porque dexamos sus fijas, 'that we left his daughters', the clause put first. aun, 'still, even now'. nos repentimos, 'we repent' (repentirse). mientra que, 'while'; bivan, present subjunctive of bivir (= vivir). sospiros = suspiros, 'sighs'. se[e]r les ha retraydo: the split future of ser with les between, = les será retraído, 'it will be cast up to them'; se[e]r with Pidal's restored e, the old two-syllable form. retraer, 'reproach, throw in one's face', as at vv. 2546, 2555, where the Infantes feared it for themselves. Pidal's note to v. 3359: 'la afrenta que les hemos hecho se la echarán siempre en cara' — '"the affront we have done them will always be thrown in their faces"'.

sentences.t:
Esto lidiaré a tod el más ardido:
que por que las dexamos ondrados somos [venidos].”
sentences.l:
This I-will-fight against all the most bold:
that because them we-left honoured we-are [come].”
sentences.i: This I will maintain in combat against the boldest man of all: that in leaving them we have come away with honour.”
sentences.n: 3359b is Pidal's own number. Esto lidiaré, 'this I will fight', the challenge formula (Pidal's note to v. 3344 cites this line). a tod el más ardido, 'against anyone, the boldest': tod = todo; ardido, 'bold, hardy'. por que las dexamos, 'because we left them'. ondrados somos [venidos], 'we have come to be honoured': venir with a participle, perfect with ser. [venidos] is Pidal's (in italics). Pidal's note to v. 3360 reads mismos, ripio, igual que en 847 — '"mismos", a filler, as at v. 847' (qué bien pago a s[o]s vassallos mismos). The footnote glosses a word mismos that the line as printed does not have, while the line-end venidos is in italics, Pidal's own supply; both words fit the í-o assonance. The note must refer to a reading mismos at this place (in the manuscript or in an earlier text of his) that Pidal has replaced, but this page does not say which, and the restored venidos is what we translate. Uncertain. The speech ends; Diego answers the charge of menos valer but takes up no challenge.

sentences.t:
Martín Antolínez en pie se f[o] levanta[r];
“Calla, alevoso, boca sin verdad!
sentences.l:
Martín Antolínez on foot himself went to-raise;
“Be-silent, treacherous-one, mouth without truth!
sentences.i: Martín Antolínez rose to his feet: “Be silent, you treacherous man, mouth without truth!
sentences.n: Tirada 146 (assonance á) — Martín Antolínez challenges Diego González (Pidal: Martín Antolínez reta a Diego González). The line-ends run levanta[r], verdad, olbidar, corral, lagar, brial, al …: stressed á, with á-e in dexastes, valen. Martín Antolínez, the Çid's man of Burgos since the poem's first tiradas, the second of the three challengers (Pidal's note to v. 3308). se f[o] levanta[r], 'went to rise', ir + infinitive making a plain past, 'rose'; the o and the r are Pidal's. Calla, 'be silent', imperative, with tú. alevoso, 'treacherous, faithless' (from aleve, 'treachery'), kept apart from traidor 'traitor'. boca sin verdad, 'mouth without truth'.

sentences.i: The business of the lion you ought not to forget: you went out by the door, you ran into the yard, and went and hid behind the beam of the winepress;
sentences.n: no se te deve olbidar, 'it ought not to be forgotten by you', a reflexive passive with lo del león as subject (cf. v. 3254); olbidar = olvidar. saliste, 'you went out'; metistet = metiste + te, 'you put yourself'. corral, 'yard, courtyard'. fústed meter = fuste + te, 'you went and put yourself': Pidal's note to v. 3365: fústed meter, 'fuístete a meter' — '"you went to put yourself"'. viga lagar, 'the beam of a winepress' (as at v. 2290). In tirada 112 Diego went out by the door crying non veré Carrión and hid behind the press-beam (vv. 2288–2291).

sentences.t: mas non vesti[st] el manto nin el brial.
sentences.l: but not you-wore the mantle nor the tunic.
sentences.i: but you never wore that mantle or that tunic again.
sentences.n: vesti[st] = vestiste, 'you wore', the st Pidal's. brial, 'tunic' (house briales 'tunics'). Pidal's note to v. 3366: 'nunca más vestiste el manto ni el brial', porque los vestidos salieron del lagar sucios e inservibles, v. 2291 — '"you never again wore the mantle or the tunic", because the clothes came out of the winepress filthy and useless, v. 2291'.

sentences.t:
Yollo lidiaré, non passará por al:
fijas del Çid, por que las vos dexastes,
en todas guisas, sabed, que mas que vos valen.
sentences.l:
I-to-you-it will-fight, not it-will-pass by other:
daughters of-the Çid, because them you left,
in all ways, know-ye, that more than you they-are-worth.
sentences.i: This I will maintain against you in combat, and it shall go no other way: the daughters of the Çid, because you abandoned them, are worth more than you in every way, be sure of it.
sentences.n: Yollo = yo + te + lo, 'I … it to you', with t and l run together into ll. Pidal's note to v. 3367: Yollo lidiaré (yot lo lidiaré), 'yo te lo lidiaré', v. 3344; 'no será de otra manera', v. 675 — 'Yollo lidiaré (yot lo lidiaré), "I will fight it against you", v. 3344; "it shall not be otherwise", v. 675' (non passará por al: al, 'other thing'). fijas del Çid, put first: the subject of valen. por que las vos dexastes, 'because you left them', with vos plural: he takes in both Infantes, as Per Vermudoz did (v. 3346). sabed, que, 'know, that': the aside sabed takes the que clause as its object, with the subject fijas del Çid put before it. mas, 'more', unaccented as printed.

sentences.t:
Al partir de la lid por tu boca lo dirás,
que eres traydor e mintist de quando dicho has.”
sentences.l:
At-the parting of the fight through your mouth it you-will-say,
that you-are traitor and you-lied of what said you-have.”
sentences.i: When the fight is done you will say it with your own mouth: that you are a traitor and lied in all that you have said.”
sentences.n: Al partir de la lid, 'at the parting of the fight', when it is over. por tu boca lo dirás … que eres traydor: the confession formula that Pidal's note to v. 3350 quotes from this line; lo points ahead to the que clause. mintist = mentiste, 'you lied'. de quando dicho has, 'of what you have said': quando stands here where vv. 3313 and 3351 have quanto, 'all that', and we take it in that sense; printed so. dicho has, perfect with the participle first. The speech ends.

sentences.t: Destos amos la razón [ha] finc[ado].
sentences.l: Of-these both the talk [has] [ended].
sentences.i: Between these two the matter has come to rest.
sentences.n: Tirada 147 (assonance á-o) — Asur González comes into the court (Pidal: Asur González entra en la corte). The line-ends run finc[ado], palaçio, rastrando, almorzado, recabdo: stressed á, then o. Destos amos, 'of these two' (destos = de + estos; amos = ambos), Martín Antolínez and Diego. [ha] finc[ado], 'has stayed, has come to an end' (fincar, 'remain, stop'): ha and the ado are Pidal's, and the line echoes v. 3352.

sentences.i: Asur González came in through the palace, in an ermine mantle, his tunic trailing; he comes in red in the face, for he had breakfasted.
sentences.n: A[n]su[o]r Gonçal[v]ez, 'Asur González' (house), the n, o and v Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 3373: Este Ansuor Gonzálvez es el hermano de los infantes de Carrión. Recuérdese que en 2172-73 el poeta le pintó también con rasgos festivos — 'This Ansuor Gonzálvez is the brother of the Infantes of Carrión. Remember that at 2172–73 the poet drew him with comic strokes as well' (there: largo de lengua, 'long of tongue'). entrava, imperfect, 'was coming in'. The full stop after palaçio and the small m of manto are as printed. manto armiño, 'ermine mantle', the two nouns side by side. rastrando, 'trailing' (rastrar, modern arrastrar). vermejo = bermejo, 'red', flushed. era almorzado, 'he had breakfasted': ser as the auxiliary of an intransitive (almorzar), as at v. 3355. Epic tense-mixing: entrava, viene, era. The court sits in the morning, and Asur has come from his table, flushed from his meal (that wine had a part in it is our inference); Muño Gustioz will throw it at him (v. 3384).

sentences.t: En lo que fabló avie poco recabdo:
sentences.l: In what he-spoke there-was little good-sense:
sentences.i: There was little sense in what he said:
sentences.n: En lo que fabló, 'in what he said' (fablar = hablar, f- for h-). avie, 'there was', aver used impersonally (= había). recabdo, 'care, good sense', the glossary's 'care, precaution' (= recaudo): his words were heedless. Pidal gives no note. The colon leads into his speech, which comes with a new assonance.

sentences.t:
“¡Ya varones, quien vi[d]o nunca tal mal?
¿Quién nos darie nuevas de mio Çid el de Bivar!
sentences.l:
“O barons, who saw ever such evil?
Who to-us would-give renown from my Çid the-one of Bivar!
sentences.i: “My lords, who ever saw such a wrong? Who would have thought we should get our renown from my Çid, the man from Bivar!
sentences.n: Tirada 148 (assonance á) — Asur insults the Çid (Pidal: Asur insulta al Cid). The line-ends run mal, Bivar, picar, far, casar: stressed á. Ya varones, 'O men of rank' (ya, 'O', as at v. 3253; varones, 'men, barons'). vi[d]o, 'saw', the d Pidal's. darie, conditional of dar. nuevas, 'news, fame, renown'. Pidal's note to v. 3377, which takes both lines together: 'Oh señores, cuando se vió cosa semejante? ¿Quién diría que habíamos de recibir nobleza de parte de mío Cid?' — '"O lords, when was such a thing seen? Who would say that we were to receive nobility from my Cid?"'. He goes on: the Infantes were de grandes nuevas, 'of great renown' (2084, 2683), and could not conceive that the Çid's renown should go ahead (1881), that they should come to be worth more through the Campeador (3314), or that the Çid's daughters should be worth more than they (3348, 3369); even to call the Çid el de Bivar, after his village, has an ironic sense in the mouth of the loose-tongued Asur González (compare v. 1376, Mio Çid es de Bivar e nos de co[m]des de Carrión). Pidal prints ¡ … ? and ¿ … ! across these lines, as shown.

sentences.t:
¡F[o]sse a rio d' Ovirna los molinos picar
e prender maquilas commo lo suele far!
sentences.l:
Let-him-go-off to river of Ovirna the mills to-pick
and to-take mill-tolls as it he-is-wont to-do!
sentences.i: Let him go off to the river Ubierna to dress his millstones and take his toll of meal, as he is used to doing!
sentences.n: F[o]sse, 'let him go off': we read fosse as fuesse, imperfect subjunctive of ir, used for a scornful wish (the o Pidal's); Pidal's paraphrase is 'Váyase', 'let him go'. Whether the s is a reflexive se run in is not certain. Pidal's note to v. 3379: 'Váyase al río Ubierna a picar sus molinos'. El Ubierna pasa por Vivar — '"Let him go off to the river Ubierna to dress his mills". The Ubierna runs past Vivar'; the river, he adds, takes its name from a place, Ovirna or Ubierna, whose castle the Çid's father had won from the Navarrese and where the Çid also held lands. rio d' Ovirna, 'the river Ubierna' in English. picar los molinos, 'to pick the mills': to roughen the faces of the millstones with a pick so that they grind (our gloss of the trade word; Pidal gives only picar). Pidal's note to v. 3380: a prender maquilas, 'a cobrar maquilas'. Maquila es la cantidad de grano o de harina que se paga al molinero como precio de la molienda — '"to collect maquilas". The maquila is the amount of grain or flour paid to the miller as the price of the grinding'. Pidal explains the gibe: not that the Çid owned mills (lords owned them, and the king himself took maquilas), but that the Çid took too direct a part, like a small proprietor, in the repair of the mills and the collecting of the toll. commo lo suele far, 'as he usually does' (soler; far = fazer).

sentences.t: ¿Quil darie con los de Carrión a casar?”
sentences.l: Who-him would-give with those of Carrión to marry?”
sentences.i: Who ever would have let him marry into the house of Carrión?”
sentences.n: Quil = qui (= quien) + le, 'who … him'. darie, conditional of dar: dar a uno a casar, 'grant someone to marry', let him make a marriage. con los de Carrión, 'with those of Carrión', the counts' house; his daughters are understood. Our reading; Pidal gives no separate note, but his note to v. 3377 gives the sense of the whole speech. Pidal prints ¿ … ?, and the speech ends.

sentences.t:
Essora Muño Gustioz en pie se levantó;
“Calla, alevoso, malo e traidor!
sentences.l:
Then Muño Gustioz on foot himself rose;
“Be-silent, treacherous-one, wicked and traitor!
sentences.i: Then Muño Gustioz rose to his feet: “Be silent, you treacherous man, wicked man and traitor!
sentences.n: Tirada 149 (assonance ó) — Muño Gustioz challenges Asur González; envoys of Navarre and Aragon ask the Çid for his daughters for the kings' sons; King Alfonso grants the new marriage (Pidal: Muño Gustioz reta a Asur González.—Mensajeros de Navarra y de Aragón piden al Cid sus hijas para los hijos de los reyes. Don Alfonso otorga el nuevo casamiento.—Minaya reta a los de Carrión. Gómez Peláez acepta el reto, pero el rey no fija plazo sino a los que antes retaron.—El rey amparará a los tres lidiadores del Cid.—El Cid ofrece dones de despedida a todos.—(Laguna. Prosa de la Crónica de Veinte Reyes.) El rey sale de Toledo con el Cid. Manda a éste correr su caballo). Only the first part of the rubric falls in vv. 3382–3408; the tirada runs on into the next part. The line-ends run levantó, traidor, oraçión, aderredor, señor, Criador, raçión …: stressed ó, with ó-e in Simen[ones]. Essora, 'then'. Muño Gustioz, the Çid's vassal and messenger, the third challenger. Calla, alevoso, as Martín Antolínez began (v. 3362): alevoso, 'treacherous'; malo, 'wicked'; traidor, 'traitor'.

sentences.t:
Antes almuerzas que vayas a oraçión,
a los que das paz, fártaslos aderredor.
sentences.l:
Sooner you-breakfast than you-go to prayer,
those whom you-give peace, you-glut-them round-about.
sentences.i: You eat your breakfast before you go to prayer, and those you give the kiss of peace, all around you, you turn their stomachs.
sentences.n: Antes … que, 'sooner … than'. almuerzas, 'you breakfast' (almorzar; see v. 3375). vayas, present subjunctive of ir. oraçión, 'prayer', Mass. a los que das paz, fártaslos: the object put first, with the a of persons, and taken up by los, as at v. 3341. Pidal's note to v. 3385: das pas (so printed, for das paz), 'besas'. En la misa, cuando el sacerdote decía el pax Domini, los asistentes se besaban unos a otros — 'das paz, "you kiss". At Mass, when the priest said the pax Domini, those present kissed one another'. fártaslos = fartas + los, 'you glut them, sicken them' (fartar = hartar, f- for h-): our reading is that the breath of his meal turns the stomachs of those he kisses; Pidal glosses only das paz. aderredor, 'round about'.

sentences.t:
Non dizes verdad âmigo ni a señor,
falsso a todos e más al Criador.
sentences.l:
Not you-tell truth to-friend nor to lord,
false to all and more to-the Creator.
sentences.i: You tell the truth to neither friend nor lord; false to everyone, and most of all to the Creator.
sentences.n: âmigo = a + amigo, 'to a friend': Pidal's circumflex marks two words run together (house). ni, 'nor', so printed (often nin). falsso, 'false', with double s; the second line has no verb. más, 'more', here 'most of all'.

sentences.t:
En tu amistad non quiero aver raçión.
Fazer telo [he] dezir que tal eres qual digo yo.”
sentences.l:
In your friendship not I-want to-have share.
Make to-you-it [I-will] say that such you-are as say I.”
sentences.i: In your friendship I want no share. I will make you say it: that you are such as I say.”
sentences.n: raçión, 'portion, share' (ración). Fazer telo [he] dezir, 'I will make you say it': the split future, fazer … he, with te lo between; [he] is Pidal's (in italics). Pidal's note to v. 3350 quotes it as fazértelo he dezir, the challenger's formula: the beaten man must confess with his own mouth. que tal eres qual digo yo, 'that you are such as I say'. The speech ends.

sentences.t:
Dixo el rey Alfons: “Calle ya esta razón.
Los que an reptado lidiarán, sín salve Dios!”
sentences.l:
Said the king Alfons: “Let-be-silent now this talk.
Those who have challenged will-fight, so-me save God!”
sentences.i: King Alfonso said: “Let this talk be silent now. Those who have made a challenge shall fight, so may God save me!”
sentences.n: Calle, present subjunctive of callar, a command in the third person: 'let … be silent'. razón, 'talk'. an reptado, 'have challenged' (reptar = retar; house riebto 'challenge'): Per Vermudoz, Martín Antolínez, Muño Gustioz, the three champions of the rubric. lidiarán, 'shall fight'. sín salve Dios = sí + me, 'so may God save me' (house).

sentences.t:
Assí commo acaban esta razón,
Affé dos cavalleros entraron por la cort;
sentences.l:
So as they-finish this talk,
lo two knights entered through the court;
sentences.i: Just as they bring this talk to an end, behold, two knights came into the court;
sentences.n: Pidal indents v. 3392: a new movement begins. Assí commo, 'just as'. acaban, present, then entraron, past: epic tense-mixing. Affé, 'behold, here are' (afé, as at v. 3407), printed with a capital after the comma. cort, 'court', the assembly.

sentences.i: one is called Ojarra and the other Íñigo Jiménez; one speaks for the prince of Navarre, the other for the prince of Aragon;
sentences.n: al uno dizen, 'to the one they say', one is called. Pidal's note to v. 3394: Ojarra es un nombre basco (otsoarra, 'lobuno'), muy apropiado para designar un personaje navarro. Yéñego, hoy Iñigo, es también nombre muy usado en Aragón y Navarra. Hubo un Enneco Semenones (o Iñigo Jiménez), cuyas memorias van de 1107 a 1129, gobernador de Calahorra y Calatayud, muy favorecido del rey de Aragón Alfonso el Batallador — 'Ojarra is a Basque name (otsoarra, "wolfish"), very fitting for a Navarrese. Yéñego, today Iñigo, is also a name much used in Aragon and Navarre. There was an Enneco Semenones (or Iñigo Jiménez), recorded from 1107 to 1129, governor of Calahorra and Calatayud, much favoured by the king of Aragon, Alfonso the Battler'. Hence 'Íñigo Jiménez' in the English. Simen[ones], [del], [rogador], [es] are Pidal's (in italics). rogador, 'petitioner' (as rogadores at v. 2080), the go-between who asks for the bride: Pidal's note goes on, Los mensajeros son rogadores (v. 2080) a quienes se otorgan y dan las hijas del Cid para que ellos las entreguen a los nuevos maridos; comp. 3418, 3421 — 'The messengers are rogadores (v. 2080), to whom the Çid's daughters are granted and given so that they may hand them over to the new husbands'. Without the italic words the two knights would read as the princes themselves; Pidal's restorations make them envoys (our account of what the restorations do). infante, ifante, 'Infante', a king's son: 'prince' in the English, to keep them apart from the Infantes of Carrión.

sentences.t:
besan las manos al rey don Alfons,
piden sus fijas a mio Çid el Campeador
por se[e]r reinas de Navarra e de Aragón,
e que ge las diessen a ondra e a bendiçión.
sentences.l:
they-kiss the hands to-the king don Alfons,
they-ask his daughters of my Çid the Campeador
for to-be queens of Navarra and of Aragón,
and that to-them them they-should-give in honour and in blessing.
sentences.i: they kiss the hands of King Alfonso and ask my Çid the Campeador for his daughters, to be queens of Navarre and of Aragon, and that they be given to them in honour and with the Church's blessing.
sentences.n: besan las manos, the vassal's greeting to the king. piden … a, 'ask … of'. por se[e]r reinas, 'to be queens', the e Pidal's. ge las = les + las, 'them to them' (ge for le, les before la, las): the daughters to the envoys. diessen, imperfect subjunctive, 'that they should give', after the present piden: tense-mixing. Pidal's note to v. 3400: a ondra, esto es, en matrimonio que se considera honroso (comp. 3721), e a bendición, 'como mujer legítima' — 'a ondra, that is, in a marriage held to be honourable (compare v. 3721); e a bendiçión, "as lawful wife"' (the headword printed without the cedilla).

sentences.t:
A esto callaron e ascuchó toda la cort.
Levantós en pie mio Çid el Campeador;
sentences.l:
At this they-fell-silent and listened all the court.
Rose-himself on foot my Çid the Campeador;
sentences.i: At this they fell silent, and the whole court listened. My Çid the Campeador rose to his feet:
sentences.n: callaron, plural, then ascuchó (= escuchó), singular with toda la cort as subject. Levantós = levantó + se, 'rose'.

sentences.t:
“Merced, rey Alfons, vos sodes mio señor!
Esto gradesco yo al Criador,
quando me las demandan de Navarra e de Aragón.
sentences.l:
“Mercy, king Alfons, you are my lord!
This I-thank I to-the Creator,
when of-me them they-ask from Navarra and from Aragón.
sentences.i: “Mercy, King Alfonso, you are my lord! For this I give thanks to the Creator, that they ask me for them from Navarre and from Aragon.
sentences.n: Merced, 'Mercy', heading a petition to the king (house: 'Mercy, O king'), printed here with c. sodes, 'you are' (vos). gradesco, 'I thank' (= agradezco). quando, 'when', here 'now that, in that'. me las demandan, 'they ask me for them', the daughters.

sentences.t:
Vos las casastes antes, ca yo non,
afé mis fijas, en vuestras manos son:
sin vuestro mandado nada non feré yo.”
sentences.l:
You them married before, for I not,
behold my daughters, in your hands they-are:
without your command nothing not will-do I.”
sentences.i: It was you who married them before, not I; here are my daughters, they are in your hands: without your command I will do nothing.”
sentences.n: Vos las casastes antes, 'you married them before': the king gave the daughters to the Infantes (tirada 104), as the Çid said at v. 2908. ca yo non, 'and not I' (house: ca non). afé, 'behold, here are'. mandado, 'command'. nada non, the double negative. feré = faré, 'I will do'. The speech ends; tirada 149 continues in the next part with the king's answer (v. 3409, Levantós el rey, fizo callar la cort).
